summary: Muhammad Nasim Khan is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who earned an M.Phil from the University of Peshawar. His career includes posts at the University of Peshawar (attested 2006–2016), University of Hamburg, and the Royal Asiatic Society.

Mukund Lalji Wadekar is an Indologist. He served as Officiating Director at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 2002–2008) and Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 2008), as well as General Editor of the Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 2008).

Mukund Ram Shastri (d. 1921) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Head Pandit at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, with affiliations attested in 1911 and 1916–1918.

Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University (~1922–1925) and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), abbot of Shofukuji (~1949–1978), and head of the Institute for Zen Studies (1964).

Mun-keat Choong is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute, Komazawa University (BA ~1986–1990), and the University of Queensland, where he earned an MA and PhD (~1991–1998) under Roderick S. Bucknell.

Munenobu Sakurai (b. 1961) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1986–1991). He served as an assistant professor at Iwate University (~1993–2001) and professor at Tohoku University (~2001).

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kyoto University and Harvard University (PhD ~1971–1974). He held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1979–1987) and Kyoto University, where he was a professor (~1990–2009).

Muneyoshi Yanagi (1889–1961) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki around 1909 and completed his studies at the University of Tokyo between ~1910 and 1913.

Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar in religious studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall at the University of Vienna, where she earned her Dr.phil. (attested 2010).

Munish Chandra Joshi (1935–2007) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (~1989–1990) and Member Secretary at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (~1994–2000).

Murray Barnson Emeneau (1904–2005) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale (PhD 1931) under Franklin Edgerton and Edward Sapir. He taught at Yale and served as professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at UC Berkeley (1940–1971).

Musashi Tachikawa (b. 1942) is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Nagoya and Harvard (PhD 1975 under Daniel H. H. Ingalls), he held posts at Nagoya University, the National Museum of Ethnology, and Aichi Gakuin University (~2005–2012).

Muzaffar Alam (b. 1947) is a historian and Indologist educated at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University (PhD ~1977). He taught at JNU (~1973–2001) and was named George V. Bobrinskoy Professor at the University of Chicago (~2001).

Myles Dillon (1900–1972) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at University College Dublin and in Europe. He taught at Trinity College Dublin, UCD, Wisconsin, and Chicago, later serving as Director of DIAS (1960–1968) and President of the RIA (1966–1967).
Myokyo-ni (1921–2007) was a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar. She studied at the University of Graz and undertook traditional training under Sōkō Morinaga from around 1960 to 1972.
Myōsei Tatsuguchi (b. 1934) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Ryukoku University, serving as professor (attested 1987) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2015).

Myoshin Fujitake (b. 1956) is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has served as a professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and was a committee member for the Otani Academic Society (attested 2000).

Mysore Hiriyanna (1871–1950) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Madras Christian College, he spent his main career at the University of Mysore and Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1912–1927), where he was Professor of Sanskrit.

Mónika Kiss is a researcher in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She pursued PhD studies in Japanese Studies at Eötvös Loránd University, studying with advisor Masanori Yamaji (attested 2016) as well as Robert F. Rhodes and Nozomu Saito.
N. A. Gore was an Indologist. He held appointments as librarian at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1957–1958) and at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University (attested 1967).
